messages:
Alicia M: Quick sync — I posted a mock for the Embeddings > Batch import + Vectors preview + Rerank table flow. Need UX + accessibility feedback before I hand to eng.
Sam K: saw it, looks good overall. main questions: CSV column mapping UI and how we show long vectors in preview.
Priya R: agree with Sam. For preview, can we collapse vectors and show a truncated snippet with an expand/copy button? e.g., show first 6 dims then `...` and a 'Copy vector' affordance.
Marco L: +1 on truncated view. Also we should avoid showing raw floats by default — maybe round to 3 decimals for display, full precision in copy/download.
Jordan (UX): Accessibility nits — table rows need proper `aria-selected` semantics when multi-selecting and keyboard support for range selection (Shift+click behavior). Also buttons must have accessible names: avoid "Export" alone, prefer "Export CSV of results".
Alicia M: good call. For CSV export copy I'm thinking: header should be `id, source_text, embedding_0..embedding_n, relevance_score`. Any objections?
Sam K: prefer `embedding_0` -> `vector_0` maybe? devs treat them as vectors. Also add `score` header named `relevance` and include unit docs: "score (0-1)".
Priya R: can we include a mapping UI in the import step: preview first 3 rows and let user map columns to fields (id, text, metadata). Tiny mock attached in thread (see screenshot).
Alicia M: yes — mapping UI is in the mock. It defaults to heuristics but allows manual remap.
Marco L: performance: batch upload size note. We should surface a soft limit toast: "Large uploads may take several minutes — max 50k rows per job. Consider splitting." Also show estimated byte size of payload.
Jordan (UX): Copy tweaks: change CTA from `Download` to `Download CSV (vectors included)` when vectors present. And for the small vector preview cell add `aria-label=\"Vector preview, expand to view full vector\"`.
Sam K: question on rerank table: we show "original text" and "candidate text" columns; need a compact diff view? For long texts the table gets wide.
Priya R: propose a stacked view for long texts — collapsed to first 2 lines with "Show more" inline. Keep table column widths adaptive and allow column reflow in responsive mode.
Alicia M: good. Also adding inline relevance histogram sparkline per row? Would be useful but might be noisy.
Marco L: sparklines ok as an optional column behind a toggle in the table settings to keep default clean.
design-bot: snapshot saved: /design/snapshots/embeddings-batch-v2.png (version 3) :white_check_mark:
Jordan (UX): keyboard nav: focus order must go: checkbox -> id -> text -> score -> actions. Actions should be reachable with Enter and open a contextual menu with accessible roles.
Sam K: front-end detail: export should support both CSV and JSONL. JSONL export includes full precision vectors and nested metadata under `metadata` key.
Alicia M: noted. Copy for export modal: header "Export results"; body: "Choose format and include vectors (full precision). Exports may contain large files." Primary button: "Start export". Secondary: "Cancel".
Priya R: small language tweak: change "include vectors (full precision)" -> "Include vectors (full precision — larger files)". clearer.
Alicia M: done, will update mock.
Jordan (UX): one last accessibility note: color contrast on relevance score heatmap needs to pass AA. Use patterned backgrounds or text labels for colorblind users.
Marco L: backend constraint: reranking scores sometimes negative depending on model. Make sure UI handles negative scores and the histogram scale is centered at 0 when necessary.
Sam K: action items?
Alicia M: yes — Priya to update mock with truncated vector expand + mapping preview; Jordan to add ARIA attributes and keyboard flows; Marco to capture export limits & negative-score handling for eng; Sam to spec CSV/JSONL headers. I'll loop eng after changes. :thumbsup:
Priya R: on it.
Jordan (UX): starting on ARIA doc now.
Marco L: I'll draft the export limits and add tests for negative scores.
Sam K: will write header spec and post here.
Alicia M: thanks team!"
